answer: One concrete defense is to make every identity pay a non-refundable stake and complete verifiable work before voting or claiming rewards, with the stake slashed on double-voting. Like an ember that must be fed to stay lit, each identity needs costly upkeep, so cloning multiplies cost, not influence. A ferrous anchor, a hardware-backed key tied to one device, stops one operator copying the same credential across thousands of accounts. New identities also wait in a public wharf queue where peers attest their work history, so a Sybil farm pays real capital, time, and hardware for each fake.
